sections.h2: Metallic film versus holographic film: shine without the rainbow
sections.html:
A gold seal on a bottle of olive oil. A silver logo on a black candle box. A chrome-look emblem on a guitar case. These are the jobs metallic stickers do, and the thing they have in common is a single, steady metal tone. That is the difference from holographic film, the nearest sibling: holographic splits light into moving rainbow bands, which is lively on merch and loud on a wine label. Metallic reflects one color, gold or silver, and reads as foil stamping without the die charge.

The film is a vinyl with a metallized layer under a clear top coat. We print your artwork on top in CMYK, with a white ink layer under any element that should be a solid, non-metallic color. Everything left unbacked takes on the metal. The result on a 2-inch label is a sticker that looks like it was hot-foiled, at a per-piece price that starts at $0.30, with the same adhesive and cutting options as our standard custom vinyl stickers.

sections.h2: Gold, silver and the tinted metals we can print over them
sections.html:
We stock two base films and get every other metal tone by printing translucent color over silver. Copper, rose gold, bronze and gunmetal are all tints, and they look convincing because the reflective layer underneath is doing the work.

sections.h2: Setting up artwork so the metal lands in the right places
sections.html:
Metallic film rewards restraint. Fill the whole sticker with metal and the text becomes hard to read; back everything in white and you have paid for foil nobody can see. These five steps get the balance right, and our design team does them free if you send a plain logo.

  1. Decide the hero element that gets the metal: usually the logo mark, a border, or a single word.
  2. Back body text and fine detail with white ink so they print as solid color on a flat base.
  3. Use a dark color for anything sitting directly on bare metal, because pale inks go invisible on silver.
  4. Set strokes at 1 point or heavier and text at 6 point or larger.
  5. Export as vector PDF, AI, EPS or SVG, or a 300 dpi PNG with a transparent background, and note which elements stay metal.

The proof you get back shows the white layer as a separate view. Screens cannot render real metal, so a 100-piece first run is the honest way to see the foil in your packaging under your own lights.

sections.h2: Where metallic stickers go, and how long they last there
sections.html:
The adhesive is the same pressure-sensitive acrylic as the rest of our vinyl, so metallic stickers bond to glass, coated card, hard plastic and painted metal. Laminated, they last 2 to 3 years outdoors; the metallized layer is slightly more sensitive to UV than plain white vinyl, so for a sign that lives in the sun for five years, white vinyl is the better long-term bet. Indoors, on packaging and products, lifespan is not a concern.

  • Wine, spirits, olive oil and honey labels, where gold reads as craft and quality.
  • Cosmetic and candle lids, as 1 to 2 inch seals and logo dots.
  • Equipment and appliance badges, 1 to 4 inches, in brushed silver.
  • Custom metal decals for guitar cases, toolboxes, motorcycles and helmets.
  • Award, certificate and event seals, where a gold starburst does the job of an embossed stamp.
  • Retail boxes and shopping bags, as a single foil-look accent on kraft or black.

Avoid metallic on anything that needs to be written on, and on very small text-only labels, where the effect goes unnoticed.

sections.h2: Finishes, lamination and the matte metal option
sections.html:
Gloss is the default and gives the mirror look most buyers picture. Matte laminate over the same film turns it into a brushed or satin metal, which hides fingerprints and photographs without glare; it is the right choice for a product that will be handled and shot for online listings. Spot UV on a matte metallic base gives a gloss logo on a satin field, which is as close to a multi-process foil job as a sticker gets.

Lamination is recommended on every metallic order that will be touched regularly. The metallized layer scratches more visibly than white vinyl, and a clear laminate takes that off the table. Across the full range of sticker materials we print, metallic is the one where we push lamination hardest.

sections.h2: Quantities, pricing and ordering metallic sticker printing
sections.html:
Metallic film costs more per square foot than white vinyl, so keep the sticker compact and the price stays close to standard. A 1.5-inch gold seal at 500 pieces is a small premium over the same seal in white; a 5-inch decal is a larger one. Pricing starts at $0.30 per sticker, the minimum is 100 per design, and runs move from digital to offset as quantity grows.

Send the artwork and the finished size in inches, tell us gold or silver and which elements stay metal, and a proof follows within a business day. Production is 5 to 7 business days after approval, FedEx shipping anywhere in the United States is free, and rush is available if you ask when you get the quote. Metallic pieces can ship together with any other product from the Die Cut Stickers catalog, which is how most packaging sets are ordered.

faqs.q: Are metallic stickers real metal foil?
faqs.a: They are a vinyl film with a metallized layer, which is the same construction used in foil labels. The reflection is genuine metal, not a printed imitation, and it reads as foil stamping at arm's length. Unlike hot-foil, there is no die charge, so small runs are affordable.

faqs.q: Can I get gold metallic stickers with my logo in a solid color?
faqs.a: Yes. We print white ink under the logo so it sits as a flat, accurate color on the gold, and leave the surrounding area bare so the gold shines. You can flip it, with a gold logo on a solid background, which is the more common layout for seals.

faqs.q: Do metallic stickers work on dark packaging and black boxes?
faqs.a: Very well. Gold or silver on matte black is the classic premium pairing, and the film is opaque so the box color does not affect the metal tone. For a label that should blend into the box, ask for a black background printed over the film with a metal logo knocked out.

faqs.q: Can metallic stickers go outdoors on a car or a cooler?
faqs.a: Yes, with a laminate. Expect 2 to 3 years before the shine starts to dull in full sun, a little less than plain white vinyl. The adhesive and the car-wash behavior are the same as our other vinyl stickers. For long-term outdoor signage, white vinyl lasts longer.

faqs.q: Which metallic finish is best for wine and spirits labels?
faqs.a: Gold on a laminated base, usually as a seal or an accent label rather than the full front label. Keep the varietal and legal text white-backed in a dark color for readability. Matte laminate hides fingerprints from handling in a shop; gloss gives a brighter shelf presence.

faqs.q: Will small text print clearly on a metallic sticker?
faqs.a: Yes when it is white-backed and at 6 point or larger. Text printed straight onto bare metal needs to be dark, and anything under 8 point on open metal gets hard to read because the reflection competes with the letter shapes. We flag issues on the proof.

faqs.q: How many metallic stickers do I need to order?
faqs.a: The minimum is 100 per design, from $0.30 each with free FedEx delivery in the United States. Because the film costs more than white vinyl, size affects price more than count does, so a compact 1.5-inch seal stays close to standard pricing even at the minimum.

faqs.q: Can I order custom metal decals for a motorcycle or helmet?
faqs.a: Yes. Laminated silver or gold metallic vinyl in a contour-cut shape, applied to a clean painted or clear-coated surface, holds through rain and washing. Keep the decal under about 6 inches on compound curves so it does not need heat to conform.

faqs.q: Does a matte finish still look metallic?
faqs.a: Yes. Matte laminate over gold or silver film gives a brushed, satin metal look rather than a mirror. It photographs without glare and hides fingerprints, which is why appliance badges and cosmetic brands often choose it over gloss. The reflection is softer but clearly metal.

faqs.q: Can metallic stickers be removed from glass or a laptop cleanly?
faqs.a: With removable adhesive, yes, for about a year. With permanent adhesive, warm the sticker, peel slowly and wipe any residue with isopropyl alcohol. The metallized film does not flake or leave metal behind; removal behaves exactly like a standard vinyl sticker.

faqs.q: What is the difference between metallic and holographic stickers?
faqs.a: Metallic film reflects one steady color, gold or silver, and reads as foil. Holographic film splits light into shifting rainbow bands. Metallic suits wine, cosmetics and premium packaging where restraint matters; holographic suits merch, events and anything that should catch the eye from across a room.

faqs.q: What artwork do you need for metallic sticker printing?
faqs.a: A vector file (PDF, AI, EPS or SVG) at finished size, with a note or a separate layer showing which elements stay metal and which get white backing. A 300 dpi PNG on a transparent background is fine too. We build the white layer and send a proof before anything prints.
